scope: Claude Code user-facing features as documented on the official docs and changelog; not a Hermes or Talaria analysis.

where_legend.ui: A terminal client must draw the output or take the input itself.
where_legend.agent: The agent loop does the work, so a client for another backend gets it from that backend.
where_legend.both: The client must show or accept input, and the backend must do the work.

features.name: Tool-call display and transcript view
features.description: Shows each tool call and its result in the conversation. Ctrl+O opens a detailed transcript with timestamps and the model used per message, and repeated MCP calls collapse into one line.

features.name: Live output while a turn runs
features.description: Response text and progress appear while the model is still working. The docs describe output that 'streams in' but have no dedicated page for the display.
features.uncertainty: No dedicated page describes the interactive streaming display. Confirmed only indirectly (fullscreen page); headless streaming is documented separately.

features.name: Interrupt with Esc
features.description: Esc stops the current response or tool call mid-turn. Work done so far is kept, and any queued messages are sent next.

features.name: Ctrl+C: interrupt, then clear, then exit
features.description: Ctrl+C interrupts a running operation. With nothing running, the first press clears the prompt and a second press exits.

features.name: Queued messages while Claude works
features.description: Pressing Enter during a turn queues the message instead of interrupting. Queued messages go out when the current tool calls finish, in the order typed.

features.name: Send queued messages now (Ctrl+Enter or Ctrl+X Ctrl+S)
features.description: Sends queued messages and the draft right away. In some states this interrupts the running turn.
features.notes: Ctrl+Enter needs Claude Code 2.1.275 or later, per the page. Ctrl+X Ctrl+S works in any terminal.

features.name: Take back queued messages with Up
features.description: Up from the first input line pulls queued messages back into the input box for editing.

features.name: Edit the prompt in a text editor (Ctrl+G)
features.description: Opens the prompt in the default text editor. A setting can prepend Claude's last reply as commented context.

features.name: Stash and restore the prompt (Ctrl+S)
features.description: Ctrl+S stashes typed text and clears the input. Pressing it again on an empty prompt restores the text, pasted content, and input mode.

features.name: Clear draft with double Esc; recover with Up
features.description: With text in the input, double Esc clears it into history so Up recalls it. With empty input, double Esc opens the rewind menu.

features.name: Rewind menu (/rewind or double Esc)
features.description: Lists earlier prompts. You can restore code and conversation, only the conversation, or only the code, or summarize from or up to a point. The chosen prompt returns to the input box for re-sending or editing.

features.name: Automatic file checkpoints
features.description: Before each turn that starts with a prompt, the session records file state so edits made by Claude's file tools can be undone. The 100 most recent checkpoints per session are kept.
features.notes: Not tracked: files changed by Bash commands, most subagent edits, edits from other sessions, and symlinked or hard-linked paths.

features.name: Summarize from or up to a selected message
features.description: Compresses the conversation from (or before) a chosen message to free context. Files on disk do not change.

features.name: Background Bash commands (Ctrl+B)
features.description: A long command moves to the background and returns a task ID. Output goes to a file that Claude can read, and /tasks lists and manages running work.
features.notes: Background tasks are stopped at 5 GB of output, and can be stopped under critical memory pressure after 30 idle minutes (per the page). CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 turns all of it off.

features.name: Stop all background subagents (Ctrl+X Ctrl+K)
features.description: Stops every running background subagent in the session. Press twice within 3 seconds to confirm.

features.name: Shell mode with a ! prefix
features.description: Runs a shell command directly, adds its output to the conversation, and by default has Claude respond to the output.
features.notes: Commands typed in shell mode run outside the sandbox, even when sandboxing is on (per the page).

features.name: Side questions (/btw)
features.description: Asks a quick question that is answered from the current context without entering the conversation history. Side questions have no tools; pressing f forks the question into a background subagent that does.

features.name: Task checklist (Ctrl+T)
features.description: Shows Claude's to-do list, built from the TaskCreate and related tools. It is separate from the /tasks background view.
features.notes: On models not named in the default list (for example Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, and Fable), the task tools stay off unless opted in with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1. This is a parity gap for a new client.

features.name: Session recap
features.description: After the terminal has been unfocused for a few minutes, a one-line summary of the session appears. /recap makes one on demand. Both are capped at 400 characters.

features.name: Prompt suggestions
features.description: After a reply, a grayed-out next-prompt suggestion appears. Tab or Right arrow accepts it. Each suggestion is a short background request.

features.name: 'You should know' notes (built-in mod, off by default)
features.description: A side agent sometimes flags something you might have missed. Answer with the note's digit. It is off until you enable it with /plugin enable.
features.notes: The side agent uses the same model as the session and has no tools.

features.name: Automatic continue after a usage limit resets
features.description: When a claude.ai usage limit stops a task, the session waits and continues after the reset. It is on by default for claude.ai subscribers.

features.name: Pull request and merge request status in the footer
features.description: Shows a clickable 'PR #N' badge for the branch's open pull request, colored by review state. GitLab merge requests show as 'MR !N'.
features.depends_on: gh (GitHub) or glab (GitLab) CLI with login

features.name: Issue reference links
features.description: A mention written as owner/repo#123 becomes a clickable link on GitHub, GitLab, and Enterprise hosts. Bitbucket, Codeberg, and Gitea references stay plain text.

features.name: Spell check as you type (optional)
features.description: Underlines misspelled words in the prompt box using aspell, hunspell, or ispell. Off by default.

features.name: Emoji shortcodes
features.description: Typing a colon-wrapped name inserts an emoji and offers suggestions. Can be turned off with the emojiCompletionEnabled setting.

features.name: Hidden-character cleanup before sending
features.description: Removes invisible Unicode characters from a prompt when Enter is pressed, and shows a notice so you can review before sending.

features.name: Large paste collapses into a reference
features.description: A paste of more than 800 characters or more than three lines collapses into a placeholder such as [Pasted text #1 +120 lines]. The full text is still sent when you submit.

features.name: Transcript viewer keys
features.description: Ctrl+O opens the transcript. In fullscreen, / searches it, braces jump between user prompts, [ writes it to native scrollback, and v opens it in an editor.

features.name: Fullscreen rendering (research preview)
features.description: An alternate-screen renderer with a fixed input box, in-app mouse selection and scrolling, a focus view (/focus), and a side diff panel. Switch with /tui fullscreen.
features.notes: Background sessions opened from agent view always use fullscreen rendering (per the page).

features.name: Themes (/theme)
features.description: Auto (matches the terminal background), light and dark variants, colorblind-friendly variants, ANSI palette themes, and custom themes.

features.name: Terminal setup helpers
features.description: /terminal-setup installs a Shift+Enter newline binding in some editors' terminals. The terminal page also covers the Option key, tmux, bell notifications, and paste behavior.

features.name: Terminal bell and notifications on finish
features.description: The docs show how to play a sound or send a notification when Claude finishes, using a Notification hook.

features.name: Screen reader mode
features.description: Turn on with --ax-screen-reader, the CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER environment variable, or the axScreenReader setting. The first line printed confirms the mode.

features.name: Voice dictation (hold Space or /voice tap)
features.description: Speak a prompt and it is transcribed live into the input box. Hold Space, or use /voice tap to toggle recording.

features.name: Usage and cost display (/usage, /cost, /stats)
features.description: Shows session cost, plan usage against limits, and activity stats. The token count also appears beside the spinner.
features.depends_on: Plan breakdown needs a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan (per the /usage row)

features.name: Session insights report (/insights)
features.description: Generates an HTML report of recent sessions on this machine: which projects you use, usage patterns, failure points, and features to try.

features.name: Feedback and bug reports (/feedback, /bug)
features.description: Opens a consent dialog to send feedback or a bug report with chosen session history. When signed in to Anthropic on a first-party connection, the report goes to Anthropic.

features.name: Export and copy (/export, /copy)
features.description: /export writes the conversation as plain text. /copy copies the last reply, or the Nth-latest reply, and offers a picker for code blocks.

features.name: Diff review (/diff)
features.description: Shows working-tree changes in a side panel (fullscreen) or a dialog (classic). Per-turn views (T1, T2, and so on) show one prompt's edits, and a file's diff can be attached to the next prompt.
features.notes: The panel needs fullscreen rendering, a git repository, and a terminal at least 110 columns wide (per the page).

features.name: Permission prompts
features.description: A per-action approval dialog with Yes or No, and a 'don't ask again for the session' option when offered. Tab adds a comment to the answer. Esc declines.

features.name: Permission modes (six)
features.description: default (Manual), acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, and bypassPermissions. Shift+Tab cycles through the optional ones.

features.name: Manual mode (config value: default)
features.description: Asks before most file edits, shell commands, and network access. The UI labels it Manual.

features.name: Auto-accept edits (acceptEdits mode)
features.description: Applies file edits and common filesystem commands inside the working directory without asking. VS Code labels it 'Edit automatically'. This is not auto mode.
features.notes: The phrase 'auto-accept' in the operator's request maps to acceptEdits. 'Auto mode' is a different, classifier-based mode.

features.name: Plan mode
features.description: Claude researches and proposes a plan without editing. Approving the plan switches to the chosen permission mode. /plan and Shift+Tab enter it, and Ctrl+G edits the plan before approval.

features.name: Auto mode (classifier reviews actions)
features.description: A separate classifier model reviews each action instead of you. It blocks actions that escalate beyond the request, target unknown infrastructure, or look driven by hostile content. Default starting mode in terminal and VS Code sessions from version 2.1.283.
features.depends_on: Supported models and providers only (Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Foundry, signed-in Claude apps gateway); model lists differ by provider
features.notes: The classifier is a model call. Non-Anthropic backends do not get this behavior from Claude Code.

features.name: dontAsk mode
features.description: Denies anything that would prompt. Pre-approved tools and reads inside working directories still run. Meant for CI and locked-down scripts.

features.name: bypassPermissions mode
features.description: Skips permission prompts and most safety checks. Meant for isolated containers and virtual machines. Deny rules still apply.

features.name: Protected and critical paths
features.description: Writes to protected paths are never auto-approved, except in bypass mode. Recognized rm and rmdir commands on critical paths always prompt.

features.name: Allow, ask, and deny permission rules
features.description: Rules in settings that pre-approve, prompt for, or block tool calls. The Tool(param:value) form matches a tool's input. /permissions opens the rules dialog.

features.name: Bash sandbox (/sandbox)
features.description: Operating-system-enforced limits on which files and network hosts Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor commands can reach. Regular permissions mode prompts for sandboxed commands; auto-allow mode runs them without prompts.
features.depends_on: macOS, Linux, and WSL2; Linux and WSL2 need extra setup

features.name: Unsandboxed retry and excluded commands
features.description: Commands listed in excludedCommands run outside the sandbox through the normal permission flow. A command that fails in the sandbox can be retried outside it (the unsandboxed retry), and that needs approval unless an allow rule matches.

features.name: Credential protection inside the sandbox
features.description: The sandbox.credentials setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables.

features.name: @ file mentions
features.description: Typing @ opens file-path autocomplete. Typing letters after @ also suggests named subagents and, with cross-session messaging on, other local sessions.

features.name: Slash-command menu and mid-prompt completion
features.description: Typing / lists built-in commands, skills, plugin commands, and MCP prompts. Completion also works partway through a prompt.

features.name: Image paste into the prompt
features.description: Ctrl+V (Cmd+V in iTerm2, Alt+V on Windows and WSL) inserts an [Image #N] chip you can refer to by position.

features.name: Multi-line input
features.description: A backslash then Enter, Option+Enter (after Option-as-Meta is set on macOS), Shift+Enter (native in several terminals), or Ctrl+J adds a new line.

features.name: Prompt history (Up and Down arrows)
features.description: Recalls earlier prompts. History is stored per working directory, and submitting the same prompt twice records one entry.

features.name: Reverse history search (Ctrl+R)
features.description: Searches prompt history. In fullscreen, a dialog filters results and Ctrl+S cycles the scope between this session, this project, and all projects.

features.name: Vim editor mode
features.description: Vim NORMAL, INSERT, and VISUAL editing of the prompt. Enable with /config (Editor mode), or set editorMode to vim in settings. The old /vim command was removed.

features.name: Vim INSERT-mode key remaps
features.description: The vimInsertModeRemaps setting maps a two-key INSERT-mode sequence (for example jj) to Esc. Only user, command-line, and managed settings are honored.

features.name: Custom keybindings (/keybindings)
features.description: Opens ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Bindings are grouped by context, support key chords, and reload without restarting.

features.name: Option-key shortcuts for model, thinking, and fast mode
features.description: Option+P switches model, Option+T toggles extended thinking, and Option+O toggles fast mode (Alt on Windows and Linux).

features.name: Suspend to shell (Ctrl+Z)
features.description: On Unix, Ctrl+Z suspends Claude Code to the shell; run fg to resume.

features.name: Custom slash commands
features.description: Markdown files in .claude/commands are the older form of skills and still work. Skills add supporting files and invocation control.

features.name: MCP prompts as slash commands
features.description: Prompts exposed by MCP servers appear as slash commands. A server named anthropic-skills is excluded.

features.name: Plugin skills as commands
features.description: Plugin skills appear as /plugin-name:skill-name and match on their bare name in the menu.

features.name: Skills (SKILL.md folders)
features.description: A folder with a SKILL.md file. Claude loads a skill when it is relevant, or you run it with /skill-name. The body loads only when used, so long reference material costs little.
features.notes: Follows the Agent Skills open standard, with Claude Code extensions.

features.name: Where skills load from
features.description: Enterprise (managed), personal (~/.claude/skills), project (.claude/skills), nested subfolder, folder passed with --add-dir, plugin, and skills synced from claude.ai.

features.name: Skill frontmatter controls
features.description: Fields include description, when_to_use, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context, agent, hooks, paths, and shell. Two flags control whether Claude or the user can invoke a skill.

features.name: Skills run in a subagent (context: fork)
features.description: A skill can run in an isolated subagent. By default this happens in the background, and the result returns to the conversation.

features.name: Bundled skills (20)
features.description: Built-in prompt-based skills such as /batch, /simplify, /debug, /loop, /claude-api, /verify, /run, /doctor, /code-review, /design, /slides, /dataviz, and /update-config.

features.name: Skill usage report (/skill-doctor)
features.description: Shows each skill's context cost and how often it is used, and flags skills never invoked. In a terminal it opens the plugin manager's Stats tab.
features.depends_on: Needs feature-flag fetching; not in sessions that skip it
features.notes: Version conflict: the skills page says 2.1.252 or later, but the only changelog entry says it was added in 2.1.261. See discrepancies.
features.uncertainty: Minimum version unresolved (2.1.252 in docs versus 2.1.261 in changelog).

features.name: Skill list and visibility overrides (/skills)
features.description: /skills lists skills and lets you cycle each skill's visibility to Claude and the slash menu through skill overrides.

features.name: Dynamic context and arguments in skills
features.description: A skill can run shell snippets to inject live output into its prompt, and arguments passed after the command substitute into the body.

features.name: Subagents (separate context windows)
features.description: Claude hands a side task to a subagent that works in its own context window and returns a summary, so large search output stays out of the main conversation.

features.name: Built-in agent types (Explore, Plan, general-purpose)
features.description: Explore is a fast read-only search agent. Plan is a read-only research agent used in plan mode. general-purpose has every subagent tool. Helpers include statusline-setup (Sonnet) and claude-code-guide (Haiku).

features.name: Custom subagents (agent files with frontmatter)
features.description: Agent files define custom subagents at managed, command-line (--agents), project (.claude/agents), user (~/.claude/agents), or plugin scope. A higher scope wins on a name clash.
features.notes: Frontmatter fields include name, description, tools, disallowedTools, model, permissionMode, maxTurns, skills, mcpServers, hooks, memory, background, omitClaudeMd, effort, isolation, color, and initialPrompt.

features.name: Subagent model choice
features.description: A subagent's model comes from its definition, a per-call choice, the CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL setting, or the main model, in a documented order.

features.name: Foreground and background subagents
features.description: A subagent can run in the foreground (you wait) or in the background (you keep working and the result arrives when done).

features.name: Forks (/subtask, /fork, fork mode)
features.description: A fork inherits the whole conversation. /subtask starts one in the background. Fork mode lets Claude start forks on its own.

features.name: Concurrent subagent limit (default 20)
features.description: Spawning another subagent fails while 20 are running. Raise it with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS. Ultracode sessions are exempt.

features.name: Nested subagents (depth limit)
features.description: Subagents can start their own subagents, up to a depth limit.
features.uncertainty: The numeric depth limit was not read from the page.

features.name: Subagent persistent memory
features.description: A subagent can keep its own auto memory directory through its memory field.

features.name: Resume a finished subagent by name or ID
features.description: A finished subagent can be resumed by sending it a message. Resuming does not check the concurrency limit.

features.name: Agent view (claude agents)
features.description: One screen that lists background sessions by state (needs input, working, completed). You can dispatch new sessions, peek with Space, attach with Enter or the right arrow, and detach with the left arrow.
features.notes: Runs on the local machine and stops if the machine shuts down. Each session uses subscription quota on its own. Edits move into a worktree under .claude/worktrees.

features.name: Background sessions (--bg, /background)
features.description: Start a session in the background with claude --bg, or move a running session there with /background (alias /bg) or the left arrow. It keeps running without a terminal attached.

features.name: Background-session supervisor (claude daemon)
features.description: A local supervisor process hosts background sessions. claude daemon status, logs, run, and stop manage it.

features.name: Manage background sessions from the shell (claude attach, logs, respawn, rm, stop)
features.description: Scripts can list sessions with claude agents --json, attach, read logs, restart, remove, or stop them.

features.name: Monitor tool (background watcher)
features.description: Runs a command in the background and feeds each output line back to Claude, so it can react to log entries or polled status mid-task.

features.name: Background task list (/tasks)
features.description: Lists background work in the session, including finished subagents, with options to check, attach, teleport, or stop each item.

features.name: Agent teams (experimental)
features.description: A lead session coordinates teammate sessions with a shared task list and direct messages. Off unless CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 is set.

features.name: Agent team display modes
features.description: In-process mode keeps all teammates in the main terminal (switch with arrow keys). Split-pane mode gives each teammate a pane in tmux or iTerm2.

features.name: Cross-session messaging (SendMessage, ListAgents)
features.description: Claude Code sessions can list and message each other. Inbound messages can be held for approval through the crossSessionInbound setting.
features.notes: Requires macOS or Linux (Windows needs 2.1.234 or later, per the page).

features.name: Channels (external events pushed into a session)
features.description: An MCP server can push chat messages, alerts, or webhook events into a running session so Claude reacts while you are away.
features.depends_on: claude.ai or Console API key sign-in; Team and Enterprise must enable it

features.name: Hook events (33 lifecycle points)
features.description: Commands, HTTP calls, MCP tool calls, prompts, or subagents run at lifecycle points such as SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, PreCompact, WorktreeCreate, and SessionEnd. The full list is in the hook events section of the output.
features.notes: A client gets these only if its backend runs hooks. Hook events from the docs table are listed individually in hook_events.

features.name: Hook handler types (command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, agent)
features.description: A hook can run a shell command, post JSON to a URL, call an MCP tool, ask a model a yes-or-no question, or run a subagent.

features.name: Blocking hooks and decisions
features.description: Some hook events can block a tool call, a prompt, a stop, or a compaction, and return a reason that is fed back to Claude.

features.name: Background (asynchronous) hooks
features.description: Hooks can run in the background without holding up the session.

features.name: Hooks menu (/hooks)
features.description: Shows the hook configurations in effect.

features.name: MCP transports (stdio, HTTP, SSE, WebSocket)
features.description: Local stdio servers, remote HTTP servers (recommended), remote Server-Sent Events (SSE) servers (deprecated), and remote WebSocket servers.

features.name: MCP scopes (local, project, user)
features.description: Local servers load only in the current project and stay private. Project servers live in a committed .mcp.json. User servers load in every project.

features.name: MCP OAuth sign-in
features.description: Remote MCP servers can authenticate with OAuth. Sign in from /mcp or with claude mcp login.

features.name: MCP tool search (deferred tool definitions)
features.description: Tool definitions load on demand, so many MCP servers do not fill the context window at session start.

features.name: MCP elicitation (a server asks the user)
features.description: An MCP server can request input from the user during a tool call.

features.name: MCP resources
features.description: Resources that servers expose can be listed and read by Claude.

features.name: claude.ai connectors in Claude Code
features.description: Connectors set up on claude.ai become available in Claude Code. Organizations can set connector tools to ask for approval or disable connectors.

features.name: Claude Code as an MCP server (claude mcp serve)
features.description: Starts Claude Code as a stdio MCP server that other applications can connect to.

features.name: Managed MCP configuration
features.description: Administrators can deploy or allow MCP servers for every user.

features.name: Import MCP servers and configuration from other tools
features.description: Imports server definitions from Claude Desktop. The /import command brings configuration from OpenAI Codex, Google Gemini CLI, or Cursor.

features.name: Per-tool approval for interactive tools
features.description: MCP tools marked as needing a user answer always prompt, even under allow rules.

features.name: Plugins (bundles of components)
features.description: A plugin is a directory that bundles skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, LSP servers, executables, default settings, themes, output styles, channels, and monitors, and loads them as one unit.

features.name: Plugin marketplaces (official, community, demo, private)
features.description: A marketplace is a catalog of plugins. Anthropic publishes three; teams can host private ones. Add them with /plugin or the claude plugin commands.

features.name: Plugin install scopes (user, project, local)
features.description: User scope enables a plugin in every project. Project scope is committed to the repository. Local scope applies to one repository for you only.

features.name: Plugin manager (/plugin)
features.description: An interactive manager with Discover, Installed, and Marketplaces tabs. The claude plugin command is the shell equivalent.

features.name: Plugin and marketplace auto-update
features.description: Marketplaces can refresh plugins automatically. Auto-update can be turned on or off per marketplace.

features.name: Plugin validation (claude plugin validate)
features.description: Checks a plugin folder's manifest and components. Developer tool.

features.name: Plugin evals (claude plugin eval, plugin eval init)
features.description: Runs a plugin's test suite. Each case is a prompt plus graders, scored over several runs and optionally against a no-plugin baseline, with JSON and HTML reports. 'plugin eval init' drafts a suite. Developer tool.
features.notes: A public docs page exists. The embedded reference this unit was given says no docs page exists yet; that is out of date. Changelog's first mention of 'claude plugin eval' is 2.1.269.
features.uncertainty: Only the page introduction, the CLI section headings, and the changelog were checked, not the full eval reference.

features.name: Mods (plugins with in-process handlers)
features.description: A mod is a plugin whose JavaScript or TypeScript handlers run inside Claude Code. Mods can draw panes and bands, redraw parts of the interface, guard or change tool calls, and add commands.
features.notes: Hooks run in terminal, Desktop (not WSL), VS Code, claude -p, Remote Control, and cloud sessions for reachable plugins; drawing appears only in terminal, Desktop, and VS Code.

features.name: Built-in mods (six)
features.description: Claude Code's own features packaged as mods: AGENTS.md loading, the /diff pane, the plugin-authoring skill, a security guard for managed settings, telemetry, and 'You should know'.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: Settings precedence
features.description: Five layers, highest first: managed settings, command-line settings (--settings), project local, project shared, and user. A key set higher overrides the same key lower down. Environment variables follow their own rules.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: Settings files
features.description: User (~/.claude/settings.json), project shared (.claude/settings.json), project local (.claude/settings.local.json, kept out of git), and managed settings for organizations.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: /config settings screen and key=value shortcut
features.description: Opens the Settings screen. /config key=value sets one setting from the prompt.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: Managed (organization) settings
features.description: Settings an organization deploys through managed files, device policy, or the claude.ai admin console. Users cannot override managed keys.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: Output styles (Default, Proactive, Concise, Explanatory, Learning)
features.description: Change Claude's role, tone, and response format for a whole session. Four built-in styles exist besides the default.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: Custom output styles
features.description: Markdown files in ~/.claude/output-styles or .claude/output-styles define new styles. Plugins can ship styles too.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: /output-style
features.description: Lists output styles or switches to one. Works over Remote Control and in headless sessions.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: Status line
features.description: A customizable bar at the bottom runs a shell script you choose. The script receives session data as JSON on stdin (context use, cost, rate limits, cache, and worktree) and prints what to show.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: /statusline setup
features.description: Describe what you want, or run it with no argument to build one from your shell prompt.

features.area: 6. Settings, output styles and status line
features.name: Subagent status lines
features.description: A separate script can render the row for each running subagent.

features.name: CLAUDE.md instruction files
features.description: Persistent instructions loaded every session from managed, user (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), project (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md), and local (./CLAUDE.local.md) locations. Files can import other files with @ references.

features.name: Path-scoped rules (.claude/rules)
features.description: Topic rule files can be limited to certain file paths and load alongside matching files.

features.name: AGENTS.md support
features.description: Claude Code can read AGENTS.md as project instructions, in place of or alongside CLAUDE.md. A built-in mod controls it.

features.name: Auto memory (MEMORY.md)
features.description: Claude writes notes about you and the project to a per-project MEMORY.md. The first 200 lines or 25 KB load at the start of each session. Topic files load on demand.

features.name: Memory editor (/memory)
features.description: Lists and opens CLAUDE.md files, turns auto memory on or off, and opens the auto memory folder.

features.name: Quick memory with a # prefix (removed)
features.description: The # shortcut for saving a quick memory note was removed. Ask Claude to edit CLAUDE.md instead.
features.notes: The operator's request listed '# memory' as an input feature. The docs and changelog show it removed in 2.0.70.

features.name: Compaction (/compact and automatic)
features.description: Summarizes the conversation to free context. /compact accepts focus instructions. Automatic compaction runs as the context nears its limit.

features.name: What survives compaction
features.description: The system prompt, the project CLAUDE.md, auto memory, a plan from plan mode, and up to five recently read files are re-injected. Path-scoped rules reload on demand.

features.name: Auto-compact window (/autocompact)
features.description: Sets how full the context gets before automatic compaction. Accepts a size such as 500k, or auto.

features.name: Context usage view (/context)
features.description: Shows context use as a colored grid by category, with suggestions for context-heavy tools and memory.

features.name: /clear (new conversation)
features.description: Starts an empty conversation. The previous one stays resumable.

features.name: One-million-token context variants
features.description: Models with a native 1M window (Fable, Sonnet 5 and later, Opus 4.7 and later, Haiku 5.5) and [1m] alias variants support longer sessions.

features.name: Idle compaction
features.description: An optional setting compacts a conversation that has been left idle.

features.name: Prompt caching
features.description: Reuses the shared prompt prefix between requests to reduce cost and latency.

features.name: Model picker (/model)
features.description: Switches the model and saves it as the default for new sessions. Press s in the picker to switch for the current session only.

features.name: Model aliases (default, best, fable, sonnet, opus, haiku, opusplan)
features.description: Short names that resolve to the recommended model for each provider. The [1m] suffix adds the 1M window. opusplan uses Opus for planning and Sonnet for execution.

features.name: Fable models (Fable 5.1, Fable 5)
features.description: The most capable models in Claude Code. Neither is the default on any plan or provider; select one explicitly.

features.name: Effort levels (/effort)
features.description: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or auto. Available levels depend on the model. The /effort slider also has the ultracode toggle.

features.name: Extended thinking toggle (Option+T)
features.description: Turns extended thinking on or off where the model allows it. Newer models always think, so the toggle has no effect there.

features.name: Fast mode (/fast)
features.description: Faster Opus responses at higher price. Toggling can switch models when the current model does not support it.

features.name: Advisor tool (/advisor)
features.description: Pairs the main model with a stronger advisor model that is consulted at key points in a task.
features.depends_on: Anthropic API only; not on Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Vertex AI, or Foundry

features.name: Model fallback chains and automatic fallback
features.description: Configured fallback models take over when the primary model is unavailable or when a safety classifier flags a request.

features.name: Model allowlist and organization default model
features.description: Organizations restrict which models users can select and set a default.

features.name: Usage credits and limit options (/usage-credits, /rate-limit-options)
features.description: Configure usage credits, or pick how to continue when a plan limit blocks a request.

features.name: Print-mode spend cap (--max-budget-usd)
features.description: Stops a -p run once estimated API spend reaches the amount. The check uses Claude Code's own client-side estimate.

features.name: Continue and resume sessions (--continue, --resume, /resume)
features.description: Reopen the latest session in this directory, pick one from a list, or resume by name, ID, or transcript path. Background sessions show a bg marker.

features.name: Name sessions (-n, /rename)
features.description: Give a session a name at startup or during the session. The name appears on the prompt bar and in the picker.

features.name: Branch a conversation (/branch)
features.description: Copies the conversation so far into a new branch and switches to it. The original stays intact.

features.name: Local transcripts and export
features.description: Transcripts are stored locally as JSON Lines (.jsonl) files. /export writes plain text.

features.name: Resume sessions linked to a pull request (--from-pr)
features.description: Opens the session picker filtered to sessions linked to a pull request number.

features.name: Copy the conversation to a background session (/fork)
features.description: Copies the current conversation into a new background session and keeps working here. With a prompt, the copy starts on it immediately.

features.name: Non-interactive print mode (-p)
features.description: Runs one prompt and exits. Supports text, JSON, and stream-json output, JSON Schema validation, turn and budget caps, and bare mode.

features.name: Bare mode (--bare)
features.description: Skips hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md so scripted calls start faster.

features.name: Unattended permission handling (-p)
features.description: In print mode, calls that need approval are denied unless an allow rule, a hook, or --permission-prompt-tool approves them. --permission-prompts none denies them automatically.

features.name: Streaming input and output (stream-json)
features.description: Newline-delimited JSON in and out for programmatic clients, with options for partial messages and replayed user messages.

features.name: Continue a conversation in print mode
features.description: Adds -c to -p to continue the most recent conversation non-interactively.

features.name: Agent SDK for Python (claude-agent-sdk)
features.description: Installed with pip. Embeds the Claude Code agent loop, built-in tools, permissions, sessions, hooks, subagents, MCP servers, skills, and plugins in your own Python program.

features.name: Agent SDK for TypeScript (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk)
features.description: Installed with npm. Same capabilities as the Python SDK, for TypeScript programs.

features.name: Renamed from the Claude Code SDK
features.description: The SDK was renamed from Claude Code SDK to Claude Agent SDK in version 2.0.0.

features.name: Agentic loop (model plans, calls tools, observes, repeats)
features.description: Claude reads the task, calls tools, reads the results, and repeats until the task is done. This loop is the backend's core behavior.

features.name: Alternative model providers (Bedrock, Vertex AI, Foundry, gateways)
features.description: Claude Code can run against Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, and LLM gateways. Some features (channels, artifacts, Remote Control) are not available on every provider.
features.notes: The provider list for each feature is in each feature's dependency field.

features.name: VS Code extension
features.description: A Claude Code panel with a prompt box, inline diffs, @-mentions, plan review, rewind checkpoints, resume of past and cloud conversations, plugin management, and terminal mode.

features.name: JetBrains plugin
features.description: Runs Claude Code in the IDE terminal, with quick launch, diff viewing in the IDE, selection and file-reference sharing, and diagnostics.

features.name: Built-in IDE MCP server (diagnostics)
features.description: The IDE integration exposes a built-in MCP server. Claude can read the IDE's inspection diagnostics such as lint errors through a getDiagnostics tool.

features.name: IDE connection (/ide, --ide)
features.description: Shows IDE connection status. --ide connects at startup when exactly one IDE is available.

features.name: Remote Control (drive a local session from claude.ai/code or the mobile app)
features.description: A session on your machine can be driven from claude.ai/code or the Claude mobile app. Local tools, MCP servers, and files stay on the machine.
features.depends_on: claude.ai subscription and full-scope sign-in; API keys not supported

features.name: Trusted devices (Team and Enterprise)
features.description: An organization option that requires enrolled devices before Remote Control works.

features.name: Cloud sessions (claude.ai/code)
features.description: Claude Code runs on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure, or on an organization's self-hosted environment, and keeps running after you close the laptop.
features.depends_on: claude.ai; Pro, Max, Team, or qualifying Enterprise seats

features.name: Start a cloud session from the terminal (--cloud)
features.description: --cloud with a task creates a cloud session. With a session ID and -p, it queues a follow-up in an existing cloud session. --remote is a deprecated alias.

features.name: Teleport a cloud session into the terminal (--teleport, /teleport)
features.description: Pulls a cloud session into the local terminal. /teleport (alias /tp) and the t key in /tasks do the same from inside a session.
features.depends_on: claude.ai subscription and the same account

features.name: Send a follow-up to a cloud session from the CLI
features.description: Queues a message in an existing cloud session.

features.name: Auto-fix pull requests in the cloud (/autofix-pr)
features.description: Starts a cloud session that watches the current branch's pull request and pushes fixes when CI fails or reviewers comment.

features.name: Self-hosted environments for cloud sessions
features.description: Runners on your own infrastructure host cloud sessions so the API calls come from your network.

features.name: Desktop app Code tab
features.description: The graphical Claude Code: parallel sessions in tabs with worktrees, an integrated terminal and file editor, computer use, Dispatch from the phone, scheduled tasks, and visual diff review.
features.depends_on: Desktop app (macOS, Windows; Linux in beta)

features.name: Hand a CLI session to the desktop app (/desktop, --desktop)
features.description: Continues the current session in the desktop app, or opens a directory there.
features.depends_on: macOS or x64 Windows and a Claude subscription

features.name: Dispatch (send a task from the phone to the desktop app)
features.description: Sends a task from the Claude mobile app to a Claude Code session on your desktop machine.

features.name: Claude in Chrome integration
features.description: Lets Claude drive your Chrome browser to test pages, read console logs, and fill forms. Turn on with --chrome or /chrome.

features.name: Computer use from the CLI (macOS)
features.description: Lets Claude open apps, click, type, and see the screen on macOS from the terminal.

features.name: Projects (claude.ai parallel cloud threads)
features.description: A project runs a stream of related tasks as parallel cloud sessions that share repositories, instructions, and memory.

features.name: Slack integration (Claude Tag)
features.description: Claude in Slack channels, backed by cloud Claude Code sessions. Claude Tag is the newer admin-governed version; the older Slack page covers the earlier app.
features.notes: The claude.com overview was readable. The code.claude.com Claude Tag page returned an HTML shell, not Markdown.

features.name: Where each remote option runs (comparison table)
features.description: A table compares Dispatch, Remote Control, Channels, Slack, self-hosted environments, and scheduled tasks by trigger, where Claude runs, and setup.

features.name: Dynamic workflows (Workflow tool)
features.description: Claude writes a JavaScript script that orchestrates many subagents in the background. The script holds the plan and the intermediate results, and /workflows shows progress.
features.depends_on: Paid plans, Anthropic API, Bedrock, Vertex AI, or Foundry; Pro needs /config toggle

features.name: /deep-research (bundled workflow)
features.description: Fans out web searches across several angles, cross-checks sources, and returns a cited report with unsupported claims removed.

features.name: Ultracode (automatic workflows for each task)
features.description: A session setting (/effort ultracode, --effort ultracode, or the ultracode setting) that plans a workflow for each substantive task. The keyword ultracode in a typed prompt starts one run.
features.notes: Each request uses more tokens and reaches usage limits sooner. Per-agent model choice follows the subagent model order.

features.name: Workflow approval prompts
features.description: In interactive runs, the prompt depends on permission mode. In -p and Agent SDK runs there is no prompt; the launch goes through permission rules, auto mode, or a host callback.

features.name: Workflow progress view (/workflows)
features.description: Lists running and finished workflows. Drill into phases and agents; keys pause (p), restart (r), stop (x), filter (f), and save the script (s).

features.name: Workflow limits (concurrency, agents per run, items per call)
features.description: 16 concurrent agents by default (raise to 256 with CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS), 1,000 agents per run, and 4,096 items per parallel call.

features.name: Per-agent model choice in workflows
features.description: Each workflow agent takes a model from the same order used for subagents. A script can name a model per stage. CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MODEL forces one model onto every workflow agent.

features.name: Save workflows as commands or ship them in plugins
features.description: A finished run can be saved as a reusable slash command, or distributed in a plugin, and passed input when launched.

features.name: Turn workflows off
features.description: Use the Dynamic workflows toggle in /config, the disableWorkflows setting, or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1. Turning them off also removes ultracode.

features.name: Large-workflow warning
features.description: Warns when a run schedules more than 25 agents or projects more than 1.5 million tokens. It is advisory and does not stop the run.

features.name: /workflow-authoring (reference for writing workflow scripts)
features.description: Loads the reference for writing workflow scripts: the script API, resume behavior, and worked examples.

features.name: /loop (repeat a prompt in the session)
features.description: Runs a prompt on a fixed interval, or lets Claude choose the pace between runs. With no prompt it runs a built-in maintenance prompt, and a loop.md file can replace that prompt.

features.name: Session cron tools and one-time reminders
features.description: CronCreate, CronList, and CronDelete schedule prompts for the current session. Session tasks expire after seven days and can be restored on resume.

features.name: Routines (cloud scheduled tasks, /schedule)
features.description: Scheduled prompts that run in Anthropic's cloud on a timer, an API call, or a GitHub event. Minimum interval one hour. The feature was formerly called routines.
features.depends_on: claude.ai account; Anthropic-hosted or self-hosted environment

features.name: Desktop scheduled tasks
features.description: Scheduled tasks on your own machine through the desktop app, with access to local files and tools.

features.name: Claude Code in CI (GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD)
features.description: Runs Claude Code inside CI workflows. The docs cover GitHub Actions, cloud provider setup, and GitLab CI/CD.

features.name: /goal (keep working toward a condition)
features.description: Sets a completion condition. After each turn a model checks it. Claude keeps working until the condition is met, a model judges it impossible, or an error clears the goal.

features.name: Artifacts (shared live pages on claude.ai)
features.description: Publishes HTML or Markdown output from a session to a private claude.ai page that updates in place. You can share, collect comments on, or publish it.
features.depends_on: Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan; signed in with /login

features.name: Artifacts that pull live data through connectors
features.description: An artifact page can call MCP connectors for live data, and can offer a file download.

features.name: Git worktrees (--worktree, -w)
features.description: Starts the session in an isolated git worktree under .claude/worktrees/<name> on a new branch. A name is generated if you do not give one.

features.name: Subagent worktree isolation
features.description: A subagent can run in its own worktree, so parallel edits do not collide.

features.name: Start a worktree from a pull request or merge request
features.description: --worktree accepts a pull request number, a GitHub pull request URL, or a GitLab merge request URL.

features.name: Worktree hooks for other version control systems
features.description: WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove hooks replace git's logic, so worktrees work with other version control systems.

features.name: Copy gitignored files into new worktrees (.worktreeinclude)
features.description: Lists ignored files that should be copied into each new worktree.

features.name: tmux session per worktree (--tmux)
features.description: Creates a tmux session for the worktree. Uses iTerm2 native panes when available.

features.name: Worktree cleanup
features.description: Worktrees Claude created are removed with the session in agent view. Some deletions keep the worktree.

features.name: Update and install (claude update, claude install)
features.description: Updates to the latest version, or installs or reinstalls the native binary at a chosen version.

features.name: Sign-in and tokens (claude auth, setup-token)
features.description: Sign in or out, check status as JSON, and generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts.

features.name: Setup checkup (/doctor and claude doctor)
features.description: /doctor runs a checkup that proposes fixes and applies them after you confirm. claude doctor prints read-only diagnostics without starting a session.

features.name: Debug logging and heap dump (/debug, /heapdump)
features.description: Turns on debug logging for the session. /heapdump writes a memory snapshot for diagnosing high memory use.

features.name: OpenTelemetry events
features.description: Telemetry events are emitted for activity, including a safety event for each tool call a rule, classifier, hook, or sandbox stopped, prompted, or sent back.

features.name: Auto-mode configuration commands (claude auto-mode)
features.description: claude auto-mode defaults prints the built-in classifier rules as JSON. config shows the effective rules, and reset restores the defaults.

features.name: Local code review (/code-review, /review)
features.description: Reviews the current diff or a named pull request, branch, or path for correctness bugs. Effort levels add reuse and cleanup checks. --fix applies the fixes; --comment posts inline pull request comments.

features.name: Ultrareview (deep multi-agent review in the cloud)
features.description: Runs a deep multi-agent review in a cloud sandbox to find and verify bugs before merge. Also callable non-interactively from the CLI.

features.name: GitHub Code Review (pull request review by Claude)
features.description: Several agents review each pull request, a verification step checks findings, and inline comments are posted.

features.name: Security review (/security-review)
features.description: Analyzes the changes on the current branch against the default branch for security issues such as injection and auth problems.

features.name: Large parallel changes (/batch)
features.description: Splits a large change into 5 to 30 units, shows the plan, then runs each unit in a background subagent after approval.

features.name: Cleanup review (/simplify)
features.description: Reviews changed code for reuse, simplification, and efficiency, using four parallel review agents, then applies the fixes.

features.name: Run and verify the app (/run, /verify)
features.description: /run launches the project's app and drives it. /verify builds and runs the app to observe the result instead of relying only on tests.

features.name: Team onboarding guide (/team-onboarding)
features.description: Creates a teammate ramp-up guide from recent usage history for pasting as a first message.

features.name: Feature tour (/powerup)
features.description: Interactive lessons with animated demos that show Claude Code features.

features.name: Install the Slack app (/install-slack-app)
features.description: Opens a browser to complete the OAuth flow for the Claude Slack app.

features.name: Keyboard shortcut reference (full table)
features.description: A full table of default shortcuts for general controls, editing, transcript view, voice, and history.

features.name: LaTeX math in responses (VS Code)
features.description: The VS Code chat renders LaTeX math in responses.

features.name: Copy with a block picker
features.description: /copy with code blocks opens a picker to copy one block or the whole reply; w writes the selection to a file.

features.name: Syntax highlighting toggle for code blocks
features.description: Ctrl+T inside the theme picker toggles syntax highlighting for code in replies.

features.name: Response width limit
features.description: In very wide terminals, the maxProseWidth setting wraps response prose at a set number of columns.
